Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"People treated as not being members of the household

77117 A person should be treated as not being a member of the same household as the claimant if


1. that person is living away from the claimant and


      1.1 does not intend to resume living with the claimant1 or


      1.2 is likely to be away for more than 52 weeks2 (unless DMG 77119 applies) or


2. that person, or the claimant, is permanently in a care home 3, independent hospital or


3. that person, the claimant, or both of them are


      3.1 detained in a special hospital in England and Wales, or a state hospital in Scotland 4 or


      3.2 detained in custody5


             3.2.a awaiting trial or sentencing or


             3.2.b serving a sentence imposed by a court or


      3.3 on temporary release from custody6 (home leave) or


4. the claimant is abroad and their entitlement to SPC cannot continue for any period during their

temporary absence from GB7 (see DMG Chapters 07 and 78)


5. that person is absent from GB8, other than in the circumstances described at DMG 77118, 77119 or
77120


6. a person subject to immigration control9 (see DMG Chapters 07 and 78).


    1 SPC Act, s 17(2)(a); SPC Regs. reg 5(1)(a)(i); 2 reg 5(1)(a)(ii); 3 reg 5(1)(b); 4 reg 5(1)(c)(i); 5 reg 5(1)(c)(ii);
           6 reg 5(1)(c)(iii); 7 reg 5(1)(d); 8 reg 5(1)(f); 9 reg 5(1)(h); Immigration & Asylum Act 1999, s 115(9)

Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Income of the claimant’s partner

85016 In a claim for SPC, calculate income of the claimant’s partner in the same way as for the claimant 1.

The income should then be treated as the claimant’s income 2.


Note: In SPC a member of a couple is referred to as a partner and both members are referred to as

partners3. DMG 77117.6 gives guidance that a person subject to immigration control should be treated
as not being a member of the same household. The income of a partner subject to immigration control
should not be treated as the claimant's income.


                                               1 SPC Regs, reg 14; 2 SPC Act 02, s 5; 3 SPC Regs, reg 1(3)

Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"77031 A claimant is entitled to SPC if they1


1. are in GB and


2. have reached the qualifying age and


3. satisfy the conditions to get a GC or SC and


4. are not a member of a


      4.1 couple where the other member is entitled to SPC or


      4.2 mixed-age couple (see DMG 77035 and 77140)


      4.3 polygamous marriage (see DMG 77016) where the other party to the marriage or the additional
      spouse are members of the same household and entitled to SPC (but see DMG 77140 et seq) and


5. have made a valid claim2 and

Concept role: dwp:Applicability.","text":"A limited disregard for the residence condition of the Pension Credit severe-disability additional amount, not a finding that a person is absent from the household for every purpose. Assess normal residence separately. The captured DMG 78077 categories are: a person aged under 18; a person receiving source-defined “AA”, highest- or middle-rate DLA care, standard- or enhanced-rate PIP or ADP daily living, or AFIP; a person certified as blind or severely sight impaired by a consultant ophthalmologist or treated as such; a person living with the claimant to care for the claimant or partner who is engaged by a charitable or voluntary organisation which charges the claimant or partner for their services; that carer’s partner; and a source-defined qualifying young person, or a child for Child Benefit purposes. DMG 78008 limits treated blindness to 28 weeks after regained eyesight and no longer being certified. A voluntary organisation is non-profit and is not a public authority or local authority. Named young-person definitions have age, education, training, benefit-receipt and interruption conditions; neither education alone nor being under 20 is enough. DMG 78078(1) requires first joining the household to care for the claimant or partner, with the claimant or partner satisfying the additional-amount conditions immediately beforehand, and applies only for the first 12 weeks after joining. Its commercial-payment route concerns a person who is not a close relative: payment liability runs either from that person to the claimant or partner for occupation of their dwelling, or from the claimant or partner to that person for occupation of that person’s dwelling; it also covers membership of that person’s household. DMG 78079 requires legal liability and a payment broadly comparable to a lodger’s similar accommodation and facilities. The joint-occupation route requires co-ownership or joint liability to the same landlord, with its non-close-relative condition and the person’s-partner branch. The close-relative exception requires satisfying DMG 78078(3) or (4) as well as the timing condition: the claimant or partner’s co-ownership or joint liability must have arisen before 11 April 1988 or, if later, on or before first occupation; the note uses the right-to-occupy date, not a later moving-in date.
